version.changelog:
Version 1.0.0

- Initial release of qa-skill.
- Automatically generates test cases and test steps for SwiftUI iOS projects.
- Integrates with dev-skill (for receiving code) and prd-skill (for validating requirements).
- Outputs complete test suites: unit tests, UI tests, integration tests, documentation, and report templates.
- Includes configuration options for test coverage, device, iOS version, and retry logic.
- Provides templates for test code and manual test documentation.
- Marks pipeline completion and suggests deployment after testing.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: qa-skill
Version: 1.0.0

The qa-skill bundle is a set of instructions and templates for an AI agent to generate SwiftUI test cases and documentation. Analysis of SKILL.md and _meta.json reveals no malicious intent, data exfiltration, or unauthorized execution patterns; the content is strictly focused on automated quality assurance for iOS development.

llm.summary: The skill is an instruction-only QA/test-generator for SwiftUI iOS projects and its requirements and instructions are consistent with that purpose; it does not request credentials or install software, but it assumes access to code and PRD inputs which you should provision and monitor.

dimensions.detail: The name and description say it generates tests for SwiftUI iOS code; the SKILL.md focuses entirely on scanning a project, producing XCTest/XCUITest files, and creating test docs — all aligned with that purpose. It does not request unrelated credentials, binaries, or system paths.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions describe scanning the repo, analyzing SwiftUI views/models, and producing test files and reports. They do not instruct reading unrelated system files or external endpoints. One caveat: the skill assumes it will 'receive' the code repo path / PRD — how the agent obtains repository contents (e.g., via git clone, mounted workspace, or CI artifact) is not specified; that operational detail may require separate credentials or pipeline permissions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec or code files are present (instruction-only), so nothing is written to disk or downloaded by the skill itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or credentials, which is proportionate for a pure instruction document. However, practical use will likely require access to the repository and PRD artifacts (e.g., via pipeline-provided workspace or git credentials). Those are not declared here — ensure access is provisioned minimally and explicitly outside the skill.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (no forced global presence). Model invocation is allowed (normal). The skill does not request to modify other skills or system-wide config.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: generate XCTest/XCUITest and test docs for SwiftUI iOS projects. Before installing, confirm how it will receive repository code and PRD documents in your environment (CI workspace, git clone, artifact store) and grant the minimal permissions needed. Review generated tests before committing them. If you prefer manual control, restrict autonomous invocation or require explicit user invocation so the skill doesn't run automatically whenever dev-skill outputs code. Finally, ensure dev-skill and prd-skill (upstream providers) are trusted, since this skill depends on them for inputs.
